metadata.name: bb-mechanics-lean-v1
metadata.hypothesis: Whole-career bot experiments through the five official tools show that (a) story answers carry most of the growth and almost all career-ending risk (randomising story answers for one half-year costs 10-40 points, randomising quarterly actions 0-4); (b) promotion is decided by Skill, Network and Output at the moment the review month begins, with all three needed, and each level caps every input; (c) at the entry level the review is usually lost through a single point given away in the last month; (d) answer character predicts effects on unseen stories (held-out-title R2 0.4-0.6 for risk, dignity, health, network, skill): concealing, deceiving, gossiping, cutting corners and blaming raise the three-month blow-up chance by 12-17 points; integrity costs almost nothing. A Skill that states these mechanics and gives an answer-evaluation procedure plus a protect-the-last-month rule will let the actor promote earlier and blow up less than the current champions, raising completion and mean quantitative_score.
metadata.change: Same mechanics and rules as bb-mechanics-v1 in about half the words: keeps the mechanics summary, the reject list, what builds each input, tactful handling, the month-before-review rule, the scrutiny rule while risk is built up, and short quarterly rules. Drops the turn loop and the per-input explanations of Dignity and Health. Decision benchmarks (H22-H23) showed Haiku already judges answers well on its own; the lean version keeps only what changed choices or what the model cannot guess (review timing, caps, dignity requirement, risk signal and detonators).
metadata.predicted_behaviour: Notes name the weakest input and the risk state. Story choices avoid concealing, deceiving, gossiping, shortcut and blaming options far more often than current champions. Fewer trust crises; first promotion at the earliest review in most runs; Skill-building main actions (rotation, mentorship) appear once Network and Output are at their ceilings. Defuse follows HR concern within the next Energy phase.
metadata.refutation: Refuted if it does worse than bb-mechanics-v1 on paired runs (subtraction removed something used), or if trust-crisis exits rise.
metadata.notes: Mechanics evidence and numbers live only in lab/reports/ingenieria-inversa/hallazgos.md (dev data, research only). The Skill states structure, not values: no thresholds, ceilings, weights, months or titles. Bot proxies (principles bot, oracle) are reported in the same folder; this manual itself still needs actor-controlled games.

metadata.name: x0-opus-ceiling-v1
metadata.idea_origin: T13 user request 26 Oct: Opus ceiling measurement with all general knowledge
metadata.operator: synthesis of general knowledge (measurement arm, not a submission candidate)
metadata.hypothesis: The current leader (F3 feedback-reactive, posterior Y about 60 with Haiku) is limited by two things: the player's reasoning and the policy's coverage (every family so far optimises survival only, and completed careers lose most of their missing ground on career level and wealth). Giving the strongest reasoner (Claude Opus at maximum effort) all our general knowledge in one Skill, namely F3's signal states and responses, f3-balance-recombined's strict precedence, an F8-style growth mode, the decision-relevant published handbook rules and the general form of distilled rules R1-R5, measures how far above the leader the game's ceiling lies when only legally usable, general knowledge is supplied. Expected: completion close to Opus's best observed rate and a mean quantitative_score clearly above F3's, with most of the gain on level and wealth.
metadata.change: New single Skill survive-then-climb (599 words by wc -w including front matter), rebuilt as one block. FROM F3 (f3-feedback-reactive-v1, f3-lean-v1): turn loop (observe, read events and last result first, take_action with exact choice and a short note, affordable retry on success false, stop at ending_score); risk-signal list (warning, HR, compliance, complaint, audit or legacy-problem wording, statistic warning, rising risk entry in status_updates); Clear/Raised/Escalating with step-down after a whole quarter without a new signal; Raised = Defuse legacy risk in the next Energy phase; Escalating = Defuse every Energy phase, Lay low and reduce risk as main action, no new commitments; story preference for disclosing, fixing or closing problems over postponing, hiding or shifting them; factor-targeted weak-review plan until the next review; Protect line (Health or Dignity in the lower part of the 0-10 range or named in a warning; Network and Wealth above zero). FROM f3-balance-recombined-v1: the strict precedence Protect > Risk > Review > Balance, with Balance replaced by Grow. FROM f3-lean-v1: the review plan keeps the main action even when Escalating (written as the single exception to the precedence); the parent's 'if still weak, change the factor' dropped in favour of 'a new weak grade restarts the plan' (lean's evidence: the Sonnet F3 run that switched factor got a D). FROM f8-secure-growth-v1: Grow as the default mode when no risk signal is active, no review plan is active and Health and Dignity are comfortable: Apply for a key project as main action, High-intensity work plus Prepare report materials, Skill learning when Skill stalls, story options that raise Output, Skill or standing at a bounded cost; Keep Wealth above zero. FROM findings.md (in words only, no numbers or weights): the two loss routes (dismissal after a second weak half-year review; trust crisis after risk warnings pile up) and the score gap (survivors fall short mostly on level and wealth, so once safe, chase promotion). FROM the handbook (show_employee_handbook, numbers as published): 3 Energy per quarter with no carry-over; Energy costs (2: High-intensity work, Skill learning, Defuse legacy risk; 1: the other four); one main action or none; a red-line crossing brings a warning; review and promotion window every 6 months; grades S/A/B solid, C weak, D very weak, bonus from triple base pay to none; promotion bar hidden, depends on Skill, Network, Output and level and rises with level; base pay 0.3 Wealth a month at L1 rising to 9.1 at L10; the seven published endings (Blackout, Breakdown, Broke, Isolated, Obsolete, capability dismissal after two weak reviews, trust crisis after a second blow-up). The published 'second blow-up ends the run' is used as the reason any blow-up moves the state straight to Escalating; the action effects in the handbook's tables justify 'Apply for a key project lifts all three promotion inputs'. FROM distilled-rules.md: R1 (in the second Energy phase after a C or D, the last before the next review, Defuse legacy risk plus Prepare report materials whatever the state), worded relative to the C or D that triggers it and the published six-month review cadence, never a month; R2 (every Energy phase includes Prepare report materials unless Protect needs all three points); R3 (judge statistics by trend and feedback, not raw size; Network maintenance or Build a mentorship only when Network falls or feedback names relationships); R4 (partly, see conflicts); R5 (any blow-up means Escalating at once; reassurance does not shorten the quiet quarter; no formal complaints or open escalations in stories). CONFLICT RESOLUTIONS: (1) F3's factor-targeted weak-review plan vs R4 'keep Apply for a key project through weak reviews': kept F3's factor mapping as the rule, because it is the leader's tested mechanism and R4 has the weakest outcome link in the distillation (D after weak review 2/12 vs 2/8) and is flagged as partly reverse-causal; R4 is absorbed only where the published effects make the key project a superset: for capability feedback (Apply for a key project lifts Skill, Network and Output; Build a mentorship lifts only Skill and Network) and when the feedback names no clear factor. Results feedback keeps Report results to your manager, relationship feedback keeps Repair a key relationship. Showcase results and Apply for rotation alternatives dropped as in f3-lean. (2) F3 Clear 'lift the weakest statistic' vs R3 'trend, not size': R3 wins (the handbook shows Health and Dignity on 0-10 and Skill, Network, Output unbounded, so raw size misleads), and Clear-state play is now Grow, not lift-the-weakest. (3) Strict precedence Risk > Review vs f3-lean's 'Lay low unless a review plan is active': precedence decides every slot except the main action under an active review plan, which stays with Review (Defuse in every Energy phase still answers Escalating risk). (4) F8 Grow Energy (High-intensity work plus Prepare report materials) vs R2 and R1: compatible; R2 is stated once under Always, R1 overrides Grow and the state in its one phase, Protect overrides both. (5) F3's 'Escalating: Lay low or Repair a key relationship, whichever fits' vs f3-lean's single Lay low: f3-lean's single action kept (fewer classifications). (6) f3-balance-recombined/F3 'near the end avoid unresolved risk': dropped as a calendar-adjacent trigger (f3-lean evidence of signal-free precautionary Defuse); replaced by the always-on story ban on adding risk wording. Dropped: check_latest_logs instruction (0 calls in F3 runs per f3-lean), F3 Outcome signal, F1 Act/Watch/Fine classes.
metadata.predicted_behaviour: Notes carry a state (Clear, Raised or Escalating) and the rule used (Protect, Risk, Review or Grow). Prepare report materials in nearly every Energy phase. After risk wording, Defuse legacy risk in the next Energy phase; after any blow-up, Escalating for at least a whole quarter with Defuse every phase and no formal complaints or escalations in stories. After a C or D: main action by named factor (Report results, Repair a key relationship, or Apply for a key project for capability or unclear feedback), and Defuse plus Prepare report materials in the second Energy phase after it. In Clear quarters with no plan, Apply for a key project as main action and High-intensity work plus Prepare report materials while Health and Dignity are comfortable; few Network maintenance or Build a mentorship quarters. Compared with F3 Haiku runs: more B-or-better reviews after the opening grades, earlier and more promotions, higher ending level and wealth, no rise in Blackout or trust-crisis exits; completion close to the best Opus cell (opus~100k).
metadata.refutation: This is a measurement, not a selection arm: there is no 'refuted' outcome for submission. The ceiling claim 'Opus with all general knowledge reaches well above F3' is refuted if, over at least 4 Opus max-effort runs, mean quantitative_score is not above F3's posterior (about 60) by more than the decision margin; then the leader is near the ceiling for general knowledge and further policy work has little headroom. If completion falls below F3's with eliminations by Blackout or trust crisis, the Grow mode is too aggressive even for the strongest reader. If completed runs do not show higher level and wealth than F3's completed runs, the growth mode is not executed or does not work. Manipulation fails if notes lack the state and rule, or Grow quarters lack key projects and High-intensity work, or Defuse does not follow risk signals; then the result measures the actor, not the knowledge.

metadata.name: f1-core-v1
metadata.target_failure: Weaker readers executing contradictory or unused text: F1's late-run caution overrides its own Lay-low guard, and most of its labels are never used.
metadata.hypothesis: F1's lead on Haiku comes from a small core that the actor actually executes: the Act test, repair the weakest, the story filter, Act-first Energy and a main action aimed at the weakest gap. The rest is either unused or works against that core. In 809 decisions of the 4 F1 digests, notes use the Watch and Fine labels 1% and 0% of the time, cite the Output-after-a-C-or-D rule 1% and 'spread' 0%, and Skill learning or High-intensity work appears in 0 of 64 Energy phases. The late-run caution is cited in 11% of notes from mid-run on and produced all 5 of F1's Lay-low main actions, every one at full Health, against F1's own rule 'Lay low only when Health is Act'; the weakest F1 game (Q 57.1, four Cs) took 4 of them. Keeping only the executed core (486 to 284 words) keeps F1's completion and score on Haiku, removes the contradiction a weaker reader resolves towards caution, and costs fewer tokens on every turn.
metadata.change: Kept, compressed: the turn loop; the Act definition without 'Output after a C or D review'; F1's Watch band renamed Weakest with the same definition (a falling statistic, else the lowest of Skill, Network and Output); the three story rules; the Energy order (Act first, then lift the weakest with the Health guard on Skill learning and High-intensity work, Defuse legacy risk after an accumulated or legacy risk warning, spend all Energy); the main-action rule with its Lay-low guard. Removed: the ending-rationale paragraph; the Fine band; the pointer to energy_cost, status_updates and remaining_energy; 'spread points'; 'repeat a main action only while the same gap persists'; the whole 'Across the run' section (same discipline, promotion rationale, Output after a C or D, late-run caution; the last is also wording new Skills may not use). Skill name unchanged. 284 words against 486.
metadata.predicted_behaviour: Against F1 in the same 4-run Haiku screen: no Lay low and reduce risk main action while Health is not Act (parent 5 of 5 at full Health) and no late-run or final-months caution in notes (parent 11% of notes); Apply for a key project in at least the parent's share of main actions (75%) and the same Energy mix otherwise (Defuse legacy risk about 40% of phases, Prepare report materials about 70%, Health recovery about 40%); promotion at review 1 in at least 3 of 4 runs (parent 4 of 4 digests); completed runs reach the parent's top Level at least as often; notes no longer than the parent's (mean about 124 characters) and fewer input tokens per decision; at least 3 of 4 runs complete (parent 7 of 8).
metadata.refutation: Refuted if 2 or more of the 4 runs exit early, or the 4-run mean quantitative_score is more than 8 points below the parent's 8-run mean (58.9), or the block decision places it below the parent under the dormant rule. Manipulation fails if Lay low at full Health or late-run caution still appears in most runs (the actor brings the caution itself), or if the key-project share falls below the parent's (the removed text was steering the main action). If the score falls while behaviour matches the parent, a removed rule mattered: restore the 'Across the run' section first, without its late-run line (P20 decision rule).

Base of a nested ladder: f1-core-v1 (subtraction) and f1-risk-signal-v1 (this text plus one risk rule), with the stall slot f1-status-line-v1 (the same rules as f1-risk-signal-v1 as a status line). f1-core-v1 against F1 isolates the subtraction; the next rung isolates the risk trigger. metadata.name: f1-review-risk-v1
metadata.target_failure: Early exits in real-game Claude-worker runs: dismissal for capability after repeated weak half-year reviews (run feedback says the review fell short and the next must be better), and trust crisis after repeated major blow-ups (accumulated hidden risk).
modules_changed: Energy step on legacy-risk warnings (moved into RISK)
alternative_diagnoses: Weak reviews come from low Skill or Network rather than Output, so an Output-led REVIEW mode will not lift the grade.
Blow-ups are driven by story choices made long before the warning, so Defuse after the warning is too late and only the story filter matters.
Actor execution failure (the worker ignores feedback it already has) rather than missing policy content; then the mode text will not change behaviour.
metadata.hypothesis: F1's balance rules react too weakly to the two observed early-exit routes. Two interruptible emergency modes driven only by the run's own feedback (REVIEW after a C/D grade or below-expectations feedback: Output-producing main action and spare Energy until a B or better; RISK after any risk warning or blow-up: Defuse legacy risk in every Energy phase and no shortcut, hide, delay or shift story options until a whole quarter passes without a new warning) reduce capability-dismissal and trust-crisis exits and raise completion and mean quantitative_score over F1, without making play permanently defensive.
metadata.change: F1 plus a Modes section (BALANCE, REVIEW, RISK) with explicit entry, action, exit and return-to-normal for each emergency; notes start with the mode and its evidence. F1's post-C/D Output line and its legacy-risk Defuse step are folded into REVIEW and RISK (REVIEW now has an exit condition and names the Output main actions; RISK makes Defuse repeat every Energy phase while warnings continue, instead of once, and turns 'avoid postponing' into a hard filter on story options). 'Output after a C or D' removed from Act. Remaining F1 text condensed with the same rules (Act/Watch/Fine, story rules, Energy order, main-action rule, late-run caution) to keep the bundle near 450 words; dropped: 'repeat a main action only while the gap persists' and the explicit pointer to energy_cost/status_updates.
metadata.predicted_behaviour: Notes begin with BALANCE, REVIEW, RISK or REVIEW+RISK plus a cited reason. After a C or D: the following quarters' main actions are Report results to your manager, Showcase results or Apply for a key project, with Prepare report materials in Energy, until a B or better appears; fewer consecutive weak grades than F1, and no capability dismissals in runs where the first weak grade arrives with time to recover. After a risk warning or blow-up: Defuse legacy risk in every following Energy phase (short warning-to-defuse lag, repeated rather than single), story notes citing disclose/fix/close, fewer second blow-ups and trust-crisis exits than F1. Modes exit: RISK ends after a quarter without warnings and REVIEW after a B or better, so the share of quarters spent in an emergency stays well below half in completed runs. Slightly lower Skill growth than F1 during emergencies.
metadata.refutation: Refuted if, on paired runs against F1 (and P0), completion rate and mean quantitative_score do not improve, or capability-dismissal and trust-crisis exits are not reduced. Manipulation fails if notes do not carry the mode label, if Output main actions do not follow C/D grades, or if Defuse does not follow risk warnings within the next Energy phase; then the text is not being executed (actor issue, see alternative_diagnoses). Over-defence is refuted as harmless if RISK or REVIEW stays active for most of a completed run with lower Level than F1 (missing or ignored exit conditions).
metadata.notes: Child of F1 for block 2 from the early Claude-worker diagnostics in findings.md (Early Claude-worker diagnostics, n tiny). No numbers, counts or calendar triggers: 'repeated weak reviews can end the run' and 'accumulated risk can end the run' restate the published failure directions qualitatively; grades S-D are published. Mode entry and exit use only grades, warning wording and the published quarterly cadence. Skill name kept as steady-balance so F1 vs child differs only in content. Compliance lint (with 116 known run titles): 0 errors, 0 review findings. 451 words of Skill text vs 486 for F1. P02 fold-in check satisfied: each note starts with the mode label and its evidence, and each mode states entry, exit and return. Note: tests/test_compliance.py::test_created_policy_metadata_and_size expects exactly 10 seed policies with change 'initial family seed' and empty parents, so it will fail until the test is updated to allow children; parents is a list of names as instructed, while careerlab register expects registered policy ids.

metadata.target_failure: Trust crisis (a second blow-up) and the D grades behind capability dismissal, both preceded by risk feedback that went unanswered.
metadata.hypothesis: F1 answers risk feedback by its strength, not its presence. In its 4 Haiku digests it took Defuse legacy risk after 11 of 22 risk-mentioning remarks (5 of 9 at 'piled up' or worse) and in none of the 6 Energy phases after its 3 blow-ups. 3 of the 4 games had a blow-up, one short of a trust crisis, which is how both of F1's Opus losses ended. Across the 86 Haiku digests, taking Defuse in the phase after a mild risk remark cut the rate of blow-ups within three months from 10% (9/93) to 2% (2/110); after a stronger remark it cut it from 20% (10/51) to 8% (13/154). After a calm remark it changed nothing (4% against 4%). The remark was calm again by the month's end in 86% of phases with Defuse against 34% without. Every D grade (37 of 37) came with a risk-mentioning remark in the review month. The new rule treats any non-reassuring risk feedback, or a blow-up since the last phase, as a signal that puts Defuse legacy risk right after Act recovery. It should cut blow-ups, risk-loaded reviews and D grades, and through them trust-crisis and dismissal exits, at a small cost in Prepare report materials.

Energy step 2: 'Risk signal next: Defuse legacy risk, however mild the wording'. This replaces F1's step 'After a warning about accumulated or legacy risk, include Defuse legacy risk' and moves it ahead of lifting the weakest. The note example adds 'risk signal' and the description names the rule. Nothing else differs from f1-core-v1, so f1-core-v1 against this policy isolates the trigger; against F1 it also carries the subtraction. 315 words against 486.
metadata.predicted_behaviour: Against F1 in the same 4-run Haiku screen: Defuse legacy risk in at least 80% of Energy phases whose latest risk remark was not reassuring (parent 50%, 11 of 22) and in the next Energy phase after any blow-up (parent 0 of 3). Defuse in about half or more of all phases (parent 42%), with Prepare report materials a little below the parent's 73%. Fewer months with a 'piled up'-or-worse remark (parent 11%), fewer reviews held under a risk-mentioning remark, no D grade, fewer blow-ups than the parent's 3 in 4 games and no run with two (no trust crisis). Promotion timing like the parent's (review 1 in at least 3 of 4 runs). Notes cite 'risk signal'. At least 3 of 4 runs complete.
metadata.refutation: Refuted as a mechanism if, with the manipulation executed (Defuse after at least 80% of risk signals), risk-mentioning remarks at reviews, D grades and blow-ups are not fewer than the parent's. Refuted as a policy if completion or mean quantitative_score is below both F1's and f1-core-v1's in the same block: the Energy spent on Defuse cost more Output than the risk it removed. The manipulation fails if the response rate stays near the parent's 50%: the actor still reads strength, not presence, and the trigger wording is at fault rather than the hypothesis.
alternative_diagnoses: Blow-ups come mostly from story choices that add hidden risk, so Defuse after the remark is too late and only the story filter matters (then blow-ups do not fall although the response rate rises).
The remark-review link is reverse causal: weak half-years produce both risk remarks and weak grades, so calmer remarks will not lift grades (then remarks at reviews fall but grades do not).
Defuse after a calm remark, which this rule neither asks for nor forbids, is what helped pre-review grades in the F3 family; the rule leaves that untested.

metadata.name: f1-status-line-v1
metadata.operator: recombine (cross-branch, stagnation slot): same rules, new intermediate representation
metadata.learning_goal: Does an explicit intermediate representation help a weaker reader carry out the same rules more faithfully than prose, at no extra token cost? The representation is a fixed three-slot status line followed by need, then goal, then option. The question is contrarian to P20 ('fewer reasoning steps always execute better'). Comparing this policy with f1-risk-signal-v1 (the same rules in prose) answers it for Haiku. An opus~100k or DeepSeek cell later tells whether the added structure transfers (P25/P26).
metadata.card_choice: P22 matches the symptom in the playbook's table, 'the cheap actor ignores instructions' and disordered reasoning: F1's rules exist but are skipped or reordered. P20 is already tested by f1-core-v1. P21 (one main priority) would drop the balance that transfers across actors (Problem A) and is close to f7-promotion-drive's concentration (45.2). P25 is an evaluation card that needs other actors' runs rather than new policy text.
metadata.hypothesis: F1's losses come from execution, not from missing strategy. The rules exist, but the actor skips or reorders them: Defuse after 50% of risk signals, Lay low at full Health against the Lay-low guard, Watch and Fine labels never written. A status line filled every turn makes rule execution consistent for a small model. Its slots are the Act dimensions, Risk calm or raised (F3's named signal state, borrowed as a label only) and the Weakest. A strict need order (Act, then raised Risk, then Weakest), each need mapped to its Energy, story and main-action response, does the rest. The policy should lift completion and mean quantitative_score over F1 and match or beat f1-risk-signal-v1, which has the same rules in prose.
metadata.change: The decision rules of f1-risk-signal-v1 reorganised as need, goal, option (P22). Step 2 fills 'Act: <dimensions or none> | Risk: calm or raised | Weakest: <statistic>'. The rules are grouped under the need they serve (Act, Risk raised, Weakest, Always) instead of under decision types. From F3-lean (cross-branch) it takes only a named risk state written at the start of every note. F3's Escalating mode, its Lay-low response, its weak-review plan and its step-down rule are not taken, because opus~100k plays the F3 family badly (Problem A). 326 words against F1's 486.

That agreement is higher than in F1 or f1-risk-signal-v1. Defuse after at least 85% of risk signals. No Lay low while Health is not Act. Notes no longer than F1's mean of about 124 characters, because the line replaces free prose. At least 3 of 4 runs complete, and mean quantitative_score is at least the parent's 8-run mean (58.9).

metadata.name: f1-steady-balance-v1
metadata.hypothesis: Classifying every principal dimension each turn (Act / Watch / Fine) and repairing the weakest before it compounds keeps more runs alive to month 48 and yields a higher mean quantitative_score than growth-first families, because the ending rates all dimensions together and the published failure directions are about persistent weakness.

metadata.name: f2-convert-on-review-v1
metadata.hypothesis: Early Skill/Network investment pays only if the policy never lets a second weak review happen. If the first C/D review (or feedback that the next review must improve) forces an immediate, all-in CONVERT to visible delivery that holds until a B-or-better review, plus a permanent delivery hedge afterwards, and risk signals trigger Defuse legacy risk, then the run avoids both observed elimination modes (capability dismissal after a second weak review; trust crisis after a second blow-up) while keeping F2's late Level/Skill gains, so it completes 48 months more often than F2-v1 and P0 and ends with higher quantitative_score than F2-v1 and F3-v1.
metadata.change: Recombination of F2 (stage machine BUILD->CONVERT) and F3 (risk signal states and weak-review plan). vs F2-v1: (1) the first weak review or 'next must improve' feedback is framed as an emergency and switches at once; (2) CONVERT spends every free Energy point on Prepare report materials (no High-intensity work, no Skill learning) and uses Report results / Showcase results as main action; (3) exit from CONVERT requires a B-or-better review (F2 required a promotion plus B), and after leaving CONVERT, Prepare report materials permanently replaces Network maintenance in BUILD; (4) if the next grade is still weak, stay in CONVERT and retarget the main action to the factor named by the feedback (from F3); (5) adds F3's Clear/Raised/Escalating risk state with Defuse legacy risk first after a signal, problem-closing story choices, and no new commitments when escalating; Escalating overrides the main action only outside CONVERT; (6) explicit priority order wellbeing > risk > stage. vs F3-v1: drops the Clear-state balanced play in favour of F2's BUILD stage and drops the check_latest_logs-after-warning rule. Single Skill, about 445 words (F2-v1 444, F3-v1 483).
metadata.predicted_behaviour: Before the first review: same BUILD signature as F2-v1 (Skill learning + Network maintenance, mentorship/rotation/key project). In the first quarterly phase after any C/D or 'must improve' feedback: notes switch to 'CONVERT', all free Energy goes to Prepare report materials and the main action is Report results to your manager or Showcase results; no Skill learning until a B-or-better review. After that review, notes return to 'BUILD' and every later quarter contains Prepare report materials. Defuse legacy risk appears in the first Energy phase after a risk signal (short warning-to-defuse lag, like F3) and its frequency tracks signals. Zero or near-zero runs with two consecutive weak reviews; fewer capability dismissals than F2-v1 and M3; first-review grades no better than F2-v1; later reviews at B or better more often than F2-v1.
metadata.refutation: Refuted if, on paired runs, it is not eliminated less often than F2-v1 (in particular for repeated low performance) or its mean quantitative_score is not above F2-v1 and F3-v1. Refuted as a mechanism if runs still show two weak reviews in a row after a CONVERT switch that was actually executed (CONVERT does not lift grades), or if completed runs lose F2's Level/Skill advantage over F4 (the early investment no longer pays once the hedge is added). Manipulation fails if the switch to CONVERT lags the first weak review by more than one quarterly phase, if Skill learning continues during CONVERT, or if Defuse legacy risk is not concentrated after risk signals.
metadata.notes: All triggers are state- and feedback-based; no calendar months, no thresholds. 'Repeated weak reviews can end the run' is a qualitative restatement of the published 'repeated low performance' failure direction, not a counter. 'Near the end' uses only the published run length. Grade meanings (C/D weak, B solid) are published. Notes are one line, well under the observed 1,000-character truncation. Diagnosis for P15 bookkeeping: target_failure = capability dismissal after weak reviews and trust crisis after accumulated risk (Claude workers, small n); alternative diagnosis = weak reviews come from low Network/relationships or hidden risk rather than low Output, in which case CONVERT's Output focus will not lift grades and the retarget rule must carry the recovery. Compliance lint: 0 errors, 0 review flags.

The D after a weak review followed risk that rebuilt once the agent stopped defusing: of 29 reviews that followed a C or D, none of the 7 preceded by Defuse legacy risk in the last Energy phase before the review was a D, against 7 of the 22 without it. In the decisive case (a third review after C, C) the split is 4 of 4 defused and no D versus 4 of 4 not defused and D, within every seed group and within P0 and M3. Adding one line to f3-lean that sets Defuse legacy risk and Prepare report materials in the second Energy phase after any C or D, whatever the signal state, removes that route for Haiku: no D after a weak review in a 4-run screen and mean quantitative_score at least f3-lean's and F3's.

No lean line edited. 278 words by wc -w including front matter (f3-lean 250).
metadata.predicted_behaviour: In the second Energy phase after every C or D, Energy goes to Defuse legacy risk plus Prepare report materials (Health recovery in place of Prepare report materials only when Health is low), in at least 3 of 4 eligible phases per run, with notes citing the pre-review rule even when the state is Clear. metadata.notes: Strongest rule of the Opus distillation (lab/reports/teacher-digests/distilled-rules.md, rule R1), chosen for the most consistent outcome-linked contrast and a visible mechanism: the D reviews cite recent incidents, slips or risk warnings, and in all 7 D grades that followed a weak review the HR remark reached its upper steps within the preceding half-year. metadata.hypothesis: Missed growth: in surviving careers the longest stall is the promotion out of L4. The parent reads 'weakest' as the smallest number. In both, Output then sat at 25-26 for 16 and 11 months and Network at 36 for 13 and 5 months, never higher, while Skill climbed from about 57 to 98 and to 90. Two A-grade reviews held with Output and Network at or within two points of that high did not promote (Skill 71 and 70). The two A-grade reviews that did promote came at Skill 98 and 90. The third L4 career ended there with Network flat at 36 for 12 months and Skill 86. In the 8 non-Escalating L4 quarters where Output already sat at 25-26, 6 main actions were aimed at Output (key project 4, Showcase results 1, Report results 1), each with a note naming Output as the gap or the lowest statistic. None lifted Output above 26, and they added at most one point each. Apply for rotation was chosen in 0 of 64 main actions across the 4 completed games. As advertised at L1, the game lists it at Skill +2 and Network +1, against Skill +1 for a key project or a mentorship, and Skill +1 for Skill learning's 2 Energy (lab/reports/first-review-search/*/quarterly-effects.json). So rotation and story choices are the main Skill levers, and Skill learning is a small extra. Skill learning was chosen in 0 Energy phases, including the 2 Clear quarters at the L4 high, whose 6 free points went to Prepare report materials 4, Network maintenance 1 and Health recovery 1. Across every state line of the 4 champion digests and the 5 completed Opus ceiling games (lab/reports/teacher-digests/opus-ceiling), no L4 state shows Output above 26 or Network above 36, while L5 states exceed both. The 3 that reached L5 did so after 18-24 months at L4, with Skill 89-97 at their last L4 quarter-end, and the 2 that stayed at L4 ended with Skill 74 and 82. None chose rotation. An input that stays unchanged after an action aimed at it is full: it gets no more effort unless it drops, and it is tested again after a promotion. There were 14 entry-level reviews in the digests. All 5 promotions had Output at the highest value the game shows at that level, with Skill and Network at or next to theirs. Each of the 9 misses had Output or Network below that high (Output in 6), and 2 also had Skill short. In all 9 misses the short input had been at its high after the last Energy phase, or reached it in a later story, and a later story choice took it away; on every losing choice the player's note expected no cost or a gain. Losing choices by miss: rest while work waited, at Health 5 to 9, with the work called non-urgent (4 misses); a note or record written for others, read as free goodwill or visible results (3); a side review or meeting, read as a relationship or visibility chance (2); learning on the job (1); passing up learning (2); turning down, correcting or going over a colleague, including a light touch with an intern meant to protect Output (4). In at least 4 of the 5 promotions, the same kind of loss happened before the review and a later helping or delivering story happened to win it back, so promotion was luck. The player also misreads a full input as weak. In all 6 games its notes call Network the weakest while it sat at its entry-level high, and 4 of 6 spent first-quarter Energy or the main action lifting it. Meanwhile 5 of the 6 first-review windows began with Skill or Output still short after that phase. Why the change fixes it: the champion's story rule, 'avoid downsides on protected dimensions; prefer helping the weakest', cannot protect inputs whose downsides the player cannot see, and it points the player at an input that is already full. The change gives the player cost cues that fit every losing and every restoring choice in these digests. Time away from your own deliverables lowers Output, and finishing or showing them raises it. Turning down, correcting or going over a colleague lowers Network, and helping, including or thanking one raises it. Passing up learning lowers Skill. With these cues, full inputs count as protected and only short ones as weak, so the player can fill the short inputs, keep the full ones through the run-up to a review, and deliberately win back a point that an honest choice cost. In scre-00004 the only loss before its second review was rest at Health 7, with an option to stay and finish declined; avoiding it gives a promotion by the second review, after which 4 of 4 digested careers completed. In scre-00002, 2 of the 3 losing choices before its first review had alternatives without that cost. Limit: in ladd-00001 the decisive choices had a cost on every option, so no story rule saves that career. Differences from earlier ideas: targeted-1026-201334 bans two named trades (rest at comfortable Health, learning with Skill stalled) until the first promotion, but 8 of the 9 misses include a losing choice outside those trades, and the player did not see them as trades. f7-delivery-stories-v1 (2/4, Q 46.5) ranked delivery options only after an input had fallen. This variant corrects the player's prediction of costs before any loss, at every level, and keeps the champion's other text verbatim.
metadata.change: Adds a short Story costs section saying that promotion reads Skill, Network and Output at each review, that each stops at a ceiling for the level (full), and how story wording predicts their cost or gain: time away from own deliverables lowers Output, turning down, correcting or going over a colleague lowers Network, passing up learning lowers Skill; finishing or showing own work and helping colleagues raise them. Balance then lifts only inputs that are not full, and its story rule counts Skill, Network and Output as protected, takes the honest option even when it costs one and wins the point back at the next chance; everything else is the champion's text verbatim (605 words, champion 393).
metadata.predicted_behaviour: Story notes name what an option costs Skill, Network or Output, or cite Story costs. With the inputs full, the player declines rest while work waits at mid-range Health, side reviews, notes for others and learning on the job, and picks the option that keeps its own deliverables moving. After an honest refusal or correction it takes the next helping, including or thanking option to win back the point. At the entry level, Energy and main actions stop going to a Network that sits at its ceiling; they go to a short input, or to Health recovery and Defuse. More entry-level reviews find all three inputs at their high. Promotions by the second review rise above the champion's 4 of 6 digested games, and month-24 dismissals fall below its 2 in 12. Disclosure choices, Defuse after risk signals and Health recovery stay as in the champion, so risk control and resilience in completed games hold near 74 and 100.
metadata.refutation: Refuted if, over 8 or more race games, month-24 dismissals do not fall below the champion's 2 in 12 and promotions by the second review do not rise, or if the mean score is below the champion's by more than the decision margin. Also refuted if blackouts or trust-crisis exits appear (champion 0 in 12), or if risk control in completed games falls clearly below 74; either would mean the cost reading pushed the player off healthy or honest choices. The mechanism is refuted if notes name the costs and the inputs stay at their high, yet entry-level reviews still miss promotion. Uninformative if notes never name story costs and losses of full inputs before reviews stay as frequent as in the champion's digests (at least one in every miss); then the rule was not executed.

metadata.name: targeted-1026-213147
metadata.hypothesis: Failure pattern: blow-ups of hidden risk set off by story choices that leave a problem open. In the champion's 6 latest race digests, 5 blow-ups hit 4 games, and those are its 4 lowest scores (20.5, 27.2, 39.9, 52.9, against 69.6 and 70.5 for the 2 games without one). Both early exits had a blow-up in month 12, and the trust-crisis exit at month 22 (ladd-00008) was its second blow-up. The monthly HR remark is a visible five-step gauge (doing all right, some risk, piled up, on your own, about to go off). Its big jumps come from story choices made between Energy phases, where Defuse cannot answer them. 3 of the 5 blow-ups, including the exit, came within a month of one of two kinds of story choice. The champion's only story-risk sentence (prefer disclosing, fixing or closing over postponing, hiding or shifting) treats both as disclosure or as harmless. (1) Taking a dispute about people to a formal channel. A team-culture story chain appeared in 2 of the 6 games. Its named letter to HR and leaders took the remark from calm to 'on your own' both times, and the formal investigation that followed set off a blow-up both times. ladd-00011 lost 4 Output, 2 Network and 2 Wealth; ladd-00008 had its second blow-up and was out. The notes justify both steps with the champion's disclose-rather-than-shift wording. In the repo's Opus digests the same investigation was followed by a blow-up or a trust crisis within a month in 5 of 5 cases (4 trust-crisis exits). The 2 Opus players who stepped aside instead (quiet help, a transfer) saw no rise in the remark after that choice; one blew up later that month in a quarterly phase after two High-intensity work points and no Defuse, with HR calm just before. Smaller cases in the champion's games: escalating a late peer team to senior leadership raised the remark one step in 3 of 3 games, and an anonymous tip to HR raised it two steps (ladd-00011). (2) Lowering a quality control in one's own work to save time, Health or Output: a lighter code review, a security fix accepted for later, keeping a manual process instead of building the automation, light supervision of an intern. In the champion's digests 10 of 10 such choices were followed by a rise of one to four steps or by a blow-up: lighter review 3 of 3 (ladd-00011, -00004, -00000); later fix 2 of 2 (ladd-00007 from calm to 'on your own'; ladd-00004's blow-up, taken at 'on your own' one month after a lighter review had raised it two steps); kept manual process 2 of 2 (ladd-00008; ladd-00004 from calm to 'about to go off'); light supervision 3 of 3. The Opus digests give within-event contrasts. Building the automation and keeping its gates strict ended the month calm in 7 of 7 cases (one of them the champion's); keeping the manual process or loosening the gates was followed by a risk remark in 7 of 7 (two of them the champion's). Close mentoring left the remark calm in 2 of 2 cases without Defuse; light supervision raised it in 8 of 10 (champion and Opus). Lighter reviews were followed by a rise in 9 of 10 Opus cases (the tenth had Defuse that month) and later fixes in 6 of 6. The notes justify these choices with 'no new commitments', protecting Output, or protecting Health and time. Why the change fixes it: the champion's sentence lets the player call a formal case disclosure and never names a lowered check as postponing. The change replaces it with a concrete rule for every story, in every state: a problem left open is buried risk; own mistakes and disclose incidents, fraud or legal breaches in full through the proper channel; in your own work take the thorough fix now even at a cost in time or Output, and it is not a new commitment; settle disputes about colleagues, managers or team culture directly and privately, or step aside, because HR complaints or tips, letters to leaders, investigations and going over someone's head keep them open. Its cue words match the option wording, so a small model can apply it turn after turn. Fewer jumps between Energy phases mean fewer blow-ups and trust crises, and calmer remarks in review months (all 37 D grades in the lab's Haiku digests came with a risk remark). The safe alternatives cost little: stepping aside cost about one Dignity point, and a thorough fix about two or three Output (with some Network or Health), mostly after the first promotion, where 9 of the 10 such stories in the champion's digests fell; a blow-up cost three to eight Output plus Wealth and Dignity. Limits: the other 2 blow-ups (both month 12) followed a chain in which the player took on a risky junior while risk was raised; this change does not target it. Difference from earlier ideas: f3-opus-distilled (5 rules at once, 2/4, attributed to dropping the weak-review plan) banned formal complaints only while Escalating and never named quality shortcuts; here most jumps start from a calm remark. No race variant has changed the story-risk sentence by itself.
metadata.change: Replaces the last sentence of the Risk priority (prefer disclosing, fixing or closing a problem over postponing, hiding or shifting it) with a three-line Stories rule for every state: a problem left open is buried risk; own mistakes and disclose incidents, fraud or legal breaches in full; in your own work take the thorough fix now even at a cost in time or Output (not a new commitment), since a later fix, a lighter check, a failing process kept or an unguided junior stays open; settle disputes about colleagues, managers or team culture directly and privately or step aside, since HR complaints or tips, letters to leaders, investigations and going over someone's head keep them open. Everything else is the champion's text verbatim (579 words by wc -w, champion 479).
metadata.predicted_behaviour: Story notes cite the Stories rule. In stories about its own work the player now takes the thorough option it used to decline: the complete review over leaving details to the author, fixing before release over a later fix with mitigations, building the automation with strict gates over keeping the manual process or loosening the gates, and close mentoring over a light touch. It accepts the time or Output cost and stops citing 'no new commitments' against a fix. In disputes about colleagues, managers or team culture it stays out of formal channels: it helps quietly or accepts a transfer instead of a named letter or a formal investigation, keeps coordinating with a late team instead of escalating over its head, and sends no anonymous tips to HR. It still owns its mistakes and still discloses incidents, fraud and legal breaches through the proper channel, and Protect still wins when Health is low. HR remarks after these stories stay calm or rise less. Fewer games have a blow-up (champion digests: 4 of 6), no game ends in a trust crisis, risk control in completed games rises above the champion's 78, and completion is at least the champion's 10 of 12. Energy, main actions and the first-promotion and weak-review rules play as in the champion.
metadata.refutation: Refuted if, over 8 or more race games with the same actor, blow-ups per game do not fall below the champion's digests (5 in 6 games), or a trust-crisis exit still occurs in a game where the player kept out of formal escalation, or completion falls below 10 of 12, or the mean score is below the champion's by more than the decision margin. Also refuted if the thorough options cost enough Output to slow careers: completed games end with a level dimension clearly below the champion's 44, or more games are still at the first level after their second review. The mechanism is refuted if notes show the thorough or de-escalating options taken and the HR remark still rises after them as often as after the risky options in the champion's digests. Uninformative if the player still takes lighter checks, later fixes, kept manual processes, light supervision or formal escalation in those stories; then the rule was not executed.

metadata.name: targeted-1026-214849
metadata.hypothesis: Failure pattern: hidden-risk blow-ups, above all the second one, which ends the career as a trust crisis. In the champion's 12 latest race games, the 6 with risk control below 100 (in the 6 digests this marks exactly the games with a blow-up) averaged 42.2 against 65.6 for the 6 without. None of them reached L5 (5 of the 6 without did), and they include both early exits. ladd-00008 had been promoted twice and ended at month 22 with its second blow-up. The route is common in this family: stretch-1026-200334 lost 2 of its 8 games at risk control 0, and the lab tally counts 20 of 151 Haiku race games of manuals with a Defuse rule ending there. After a first blow-up the champion lets risk care lapse. Its state steps down after a quiet quarter, Raised asks for one Defuse and Clear for none, so Defuse stops just when one more blow-up would end the career. In 3 of the 4 digested games with a blow-up, a later Energy phase had no Defuse (4 phases in all). ladd-00008 skipped it in the phase right after its second promotion and spent all three points on Network and Output, although its two previous HR remarks still reported risk, so even its own state rule asked for Defuse. Three months later the remark reached 'on your own', and the next story set off the second blow-up. ladd-00004 skipped two phases in a row around a promotion, both Clear by the state rule. The remark then reached the top step ('about to go off') two months running and then 'on your own', the closest call in the set; it calmed only after Defuse and Lay low. ladd-00011 skipped one Clear phase, and the remark later climbed back to 'piled up'. ladd-00006, the only one that Defused in every phase after its blow-up, had no second one. Why the change fixes it: after a blow-up the career has one life left, and a single story can lift the HR remark from calm to the top step within a month, faster than a state that steps down after quiet quarters can react. The lab's Haiku data say Defuse pays when risk remarks recur: after a mild remark it cut blow-ups within three months from 10 % to 2 %, after a strong one from 20 % to 8 %. Guardrail G1 asks to keep it up to the end, since 4 lab games reached the end and still finished at risk control 0. A fixed rule keyed to one salient event, instead of a state the small model must track across promotions and good reviews, keeps Defuse in every Energy phase after the first blow-up. Its cost is two Energy, up to two Output or Network points, in each phase the champion left without Defuse after a blow-up (4 phases across the 6 digests; in one of them those points had added nothing at a level high). Difference from earlier ideas: targeted-1026-213147 changes the story choices that set off blow-ups; this change touches only Energy after a first blow-up and leaves play before it as in the champion. It adds Defuse rather than cutting it, unlike observed-growth-v2, and its trigger is an event, not the calendar.
metadata.change: Adds one sentence to the Risk priority: after a blow-up, Defuse legacy risk in every Energy phase for the rest of the career, even in Clear quarters and right after a promotion, because a second blow-up ends the career. Everything else is the champion's text verbatim.
metadata.predicted_behaviour: Nothing changes before a first blow-up. After one, every later Energy phase spends two points on Defuse legacy risk, including Clear quarters and the phase right after a promotion, and the notes cite the blow-up. In the champion's digests 4 post-blow-up phases had no Defuse, in 3 of the 4 games with a blow-up; now there should be none. Main actions, stories and the remaining Energy point follow the champion, so Lay low appears no more often than before. Second blow-ups and trust-crisis exits fall below the champion's 1 in 12, HR remarks after a first blow-up reach the top steps less often, and risk control in completed games stays at or above the champion's 78. Completion is at least the champion's 10 of 12, and the level and wealth dimensions of completed games stay near its 44 and 35.
metadata.refutation: Refuted if, over 8 or more race games with the same actor, the share of games with a blow-up that go on to a second blow-up or trust crisis is not below the champion's 1 in 6, or completion falls below the champion's 10 of 12, or the mean score is below the champion's by more than the decision margin. Also refuted if the extra Defuse slows careers: completed games with a blow-up end at a lower level than the champion's (L3 to L4). Uninformative if post-blow-up Energy phases still lack Defuse (the rule was not executed), or if fewer than 4 games have a blow-up.

metadata.name: targeted-1026-221555
metadata.hypothesis: Failure pattern: the risk state does not step down, so Escalating (main action Lay low and reduce risk, no new commitments in stories) runs on through quarters in which the HR gauge is calm. The cause is in the text. The champion's Risk line counts any 'HR' wording as a signal, and every month's feedback carries an HR comment, plain praise included. It also counts compliance, audit, warning and legacy-problem wording, which most months' events contain, and the state steps down only after a whole quarter without a new signal. In practice no quarter is ever quiet. Evidence from the champion's 6 latest race digests: of 22 Lay-low main actions, 7 (final quarter excluded; 9 with it) came right after three plain-praise HR comments in a row with no blow-up, all at Health 8-10, in 4 of the 6 games. None of those notes cites an HR comment; they cite event topics (a security incident, a merge incident, a legacy service, restructure rumours), weak reviews, a past health scare or the approaching end. ladd-00004 (39.9, the worst completed game, 30 months at L2): after its blow-up at month 17 every HR comment was praise through month 27, yet it stayed Escalating for four quarters and took Lay low at Health 10 in all four (months 18, 21, 24, 27), the last three after calm quarters. Its L2 reviews in that stretch were a C at month 23 with Output 3 and a D at month 29 with Output 4-5, against an L2 high of 6. Once it switched to Report results and key projects (months 30-39) it was promoted at month 41, and it finished at L3. ladd-00006 (20.5, dismissed at month 24, never left L1): at month 9, after three calm comments, its notes still said Escalating, and under 'no new commitments' it turned down weekend work at Health 8. That cost a point each of Skill, Network and Output two months before its second review, where Output stood at 0 (the same option cost the same three points in ladd-00008). Its last main action before the dismissal review was Lay low at Health 8 after three calm comments, citing repeated warnings and weak reviews, where the review plan called for a results or relationship action. ladd-00011 (52.9, finished L4) took Lay low at months 36 and 39 at Health 8-9 after calm quarters, citing a late game and the near end; these were the two main actions before its month-41 review, which did not promote. ladd-00000 did it once (month 24). The parent f3-balance-recombined has the same Signals text and the same pattern. ladd-954bf378-00001 (dismissed at month 24, never left L1) stayed Escalating through ten plain-praise HR comments in a row (months 12-21), Defused in every phase and took Lay low at month 15 with Output 2, below its entry-level high. scre-954bf378-00003 took Lay low ten quarters in a row, three of them after calm quarters, and spent 18 months at L3. Why the change fixes it: it makes the monthly HR comment, the in-run measure of hidden risk, the gauge for leaving Escalating. A whole quarter of plain-praise HR comments with no blow-up steps Escalating down to Raised whatever the events say, and plain praise no longer counts as an HR signal. The player then returns to the Review and Balance priorities (Report results, Showcase results, a key project) and to the first-promotion guard in stories, while Raised still buys Defuse in the next Energy phase (G1). Entry into Escalating is unchanged, so Lay low still follows strong HR comments and blow-ups. Why it should be safe: in the lab's 86 Haiku digests, blow-ups within three months of a calm HR remark were 4 % with or without Defuse (B5). stretch-1026-200334 found the next HR remark calm after 22 of 26 Lay-low quarters and after 8 of 8 Report-results quarters that followed a Defuse. Difference from earlier ideas: stretch-1026-200334 (4/8, Q 46.7) removed Lay low from Escalating altogether, and the lesson was that Lay low in real escalation protected survival; here it stays whenever the gauge is up. bold-1026-211845 replaces the whole manual with a stateless recipe; this edits two lines of the champion. targeted-1026-213147 and targeted-1026-214849 work on blow-ups, not on leaving Escalating. Limits: blow-ups (5 in 4 of the 6 games) remain the other large cost and are not targeted here. ladd-00006 also turned down an on-call swap just before its third review, losing Output and Network; a mild HR comment fell in that quarter, so that case stays Escalating under this rule.
metadata.change: Two edits in Signals, everything else verbatim: the Risk line counts only an HR comment that mentions risk, so plain monthly praise is no longer a signal, and a new Gauge line makes the monthly HR comment the measure for leaving Escalating. After a whole quarter of plain-praise HR comments with no blow-up, Escalating steps down to Raised even if events still mention risks, a review was weak or the end is near; Raised still steps down to Clear only after a quarter without any new signal (527 words by wc -w, champion 479).

After a quarter of plain-praise HR comments with no blow-up they say Raised or Clear, not Escalating, and the main action follows the Review or Balance priority (Report results, Showcase results, a key project) instead of Lay low and reduce risk. metadata.name: f4-review-first-v1
metadata.hypothesis: The dominant early exit for LLM actors is dismissal after repeated weak half-year reviews, not burnout. A less defensive, single-priority policy that aims every half-year at a strong review through Output-producing Energy and Report results to your manager, and leaves that priority only when Health or Dignity is clearly in danger (lower part of the range or named in a warning), Network is at or near zero, or a risk warning appears, gets fewer C/D grades, fewer capability dismissals, a higher completion rate and a higher mean quantitative_score than its parent F4 and than P0.
metadata.change: Versus f4-visible-delivery-v1: (1) the wellbeing floor is narrowed to 'clearly in danger' - the falling-trend trigger, the generic 'any warning about health, burnout, conduct, standing or risk' trigger and the Wealth-below-zero trigger are removed, and a slow decline is explicitly not an exception; (2) the four-way main-action menu (Showcase / Report / Fight for resources / Apply for a key project) collapses to one default, Report results to your manager, with Apply for a key project only when feedback points to capability or Skill stalls; (3) risk warnings get a single dedicated exception (Defuse legacy risk next Energy phase) instead of being folded into the floor; (4) a C or D review, or feedback that results fell short, makes the next review an explicit emergency in which every spare Energy point and the main action go to Output and reporting aimed at the named gap; (5) story-event rule adds an explicit ban on shortcuts that build hidden risk. Same note-mode convention (P02). Skill text stays the same size as the parent (429 vs 424 words, front matter included): fewer floor triggers and menu items, offset by the explicit exceptions and review-emergency rule.
metadata.predicted_behaviour: Higher share of Prepare report materials and High-intensity work and lower share of recovery actions than F4 and F1; Report results to your manager as the main action in most quarters, with Apply for a key project appearing after capability feedback; recovery only in short bursts when Health or Dignity reaches the lower part of the range, not on a slow decline; Defuse legacy risk concentrated right after risk warnings; after a C or D, the following two quarterly phases are all Output-producing; notes start with 'deliver', 'review emergency' or 'exception: <dimension>'. Outcome: fewer C/D grades and fewer 'dismissed for capability' exits than F4/P0/M3, possibly lower end-of-run Health/Dignity and more health-direction exits.
metadata.refutation: Refuted if, on paired runs against F4 and P0 with the same actor, f4-review-first-v1 does not reduce the rate of C/D reviews or of capability dismissals, or its completion rate and mean quantitative_score are not higher. Refuted in its premise if it trades capability dismissals for health/dignity or trust-crisis exits at an equal or higher total elimination rate (burnout or hidden risk, not weak reviews, then becomes the binding failure). Manipulation fails if its Output-action share and its recovery share are not clearly different from F4's, or if notes rarely carry the mode label.
metadata.target_failure: dismissed for capability after repeated weak half-year reviews
metadata.trajectory_signature: run's own review feedback shows weak grades (C, then C or D) with text saying the review fell short, followed by a capability dismissal at a review point; recovery or balanced actions were chosen in quarters where no dimension was in danger
alternative_diagnoses: Weak reviews come from hidden factors the visible statistics do not show (e.g. accumulated risk or Skill lagging level expectations), so more Output will not lift the grade.
The actor ignores existing delivery rules (execution failure, problem A), so a stronger rule set will not change behaviour; a shorter text might.
Burnout-side exits are merely masked by earlier dismissals; removing defence will expose them.
metadata.notes: Contrarian child generated from the early Claude-worker diagnostic (findings.md, 26 Oct: capability dismissals at the review point after C, C, D feedback; trust-crisis exits after repeated blow-ups) rather than from the P10 trigger ('survives without progress'), which has not fired; P21 supplies the one-dominant-priority-with-few-exceptions shape. All conditions are qualitative and come from the run's own state, warnings and review feedback: no thresholds, counts, calendar triggers or named events. The risk-warning exception and the anti-shortcut story rule are kept deliberately so that 'less defensive' does not mean ignoring real warnings (the P10 card's own condition) and does not feed the trust-crisis exit. Notes stay short and mode-first, well under the 1,000-character note limit.

A temporary single priority (P12) - while the latest review did not promote you, take the story option that best shows delivered results or raises standing with decision makers at a bounded cost, with Apply for a key project as main action, and only Health, Dignity, Wealth and risk warnings as exceptions - brings the first promotion earlier than the leader's balanced rules. f8-secure-growth, whose Grow mode played this way before its first review, was promoted at review 1 in 3 of 4 Haiku games against 14 of 38 overall.

metadata.learning_goal: Find out whether the bottleneck the traces point to (leaving the starting level; every B after the first review came at Level 2 or above) responds to concentration: does a feedback-gated single priority on delivered results and standing bring the first promotion earlier than the leader's balanced, risk-first rules, and what does it cost in Network, risk warnings and trust crises? Main action Apply for a key project in at least 90% of drive quarters; Lay low only with Health at risk. metadata.hypothesis: Reviews reward Output and Network being at their recent high when the review lands: across 127 reviews at Level 1-2, a B or a promotion followed 33 of 62 reviews with both at their high, 9 of 24 with Output only, 6 of 28 with Network only and 1 of 13 with neither; every one of the 14 first-review promotions had Output at its high (12 of 24 non-promoted games did not). Marking Skill, Network and Output at risk only when below their recent high makes the leader's own story rule 1 shield a stat that fell, its Energy rule restore it, and its main action default to a key project, so more reviews find Output and Network at their high.

After a fall, the next Energy phase restores it (Prepare report materials or Network maintenance) in at least 3 of 4 cases; main action Apply for a key project whenever nothing is still at risk; Report results/Showcase only to cover a fallen stat. metadata.name: f8-secure-growth-v1
metadata.idea_origin: playbook:P10 (less defensive family that keeps its response to warnings), chosen because the stall trigger fires and because of the score-gap finding in findings.md (strategy-session request, 26 Oct ~14:45 UTC)
metadata.operator: new family seeded from the F3 core (cross-branch hypothesis under the stagnation rule)
metadata.hypothesis: Completed games already survive; the score they leave on the table is mostly career level and wealth (findings.md, 48 completed games, all actors), and every family so far optimises survival. F3's Clear state spends quiet quarters lifting the weakest statistic, which keeps the agent safe but does not compete for promotion. A policy that keeps F3's risk response (Secure) and weak-review plan (Repair) with higher precedence, and otherwise plays for promotion and pay (Grow: Apply for a key project, High-intensity work plus Prepare report materials while Health is comfortable, story options that raise Output, Skill, Wealth or standing at a bounded cost), will earn more A or S reviews, hence more promotions and salary, and end with higher level and wealth dimensions than F3 and f3-lean without more eliminations.
metadata.change: New family. Reuses f3-lean's turn loop, risk-signal list, Raised/Escalating responses (merged into one Secure mode with Defuse first in the next Energy phase and every Energy phase while signals repeat, story preference for disclose/fix/close, exit after a whole quarter without a new signal) and the weak review plan (Repair). Recovery becomes the first mode. F3's Clear state ('best visible trade-off; lift the weakest statistic') is replaced by Grow. Dropped from f3-lean: Lay low and reduce risk as the Escalating main action (Secure keeps Defuse in Energy, the main action stays with Repair or Grow) and the explicit no-new-commitments clause. Added: Keep Wealth above zero.
metadata.learning_goal: Does pushing for promotion and pay in quiet periods raise level and wealth enough to beat the survival-only F3 family, or does it add eliminations (health, trust crisis) that cancel the gain? This is the stagnation slot's contrarian question: is the F3 family too defensive when there are no warnings?
metadata.predicted_behaviour: Notes start with Recover, Secure, Repair or Grow. Before the first review and in quarters after B or better reviews without risk signals, the main action is Apply for a key project or Showcase results and Energy goes to High-intensity work plus Prepare report materials. After a risk signal, Defuse legacy risk in the next Energy phase. After a C or D, the main action follows the factor named until the next review. Compared with F3-family Haiku runs: more High-intensity work and key projects, fewer Network maintenance and Lay low quarters, more A grades in the second half of the run, a higher ending level and wealth, and a similar completion rate.
metadata.refutation: Refuted if, on 4 or more Haiku runs, posterior Y is not above f3-lean's and F3's, or completion falls below theirs, or the ending level and wealth dimensions are not higher than the F3 family's completed runs. Harmful if eliminations by health, burnout or trust crisis appear that F3-family runs did not show (Grow is then too aggressive; next step is a gentler Grow, not more rules). Manipulation fails if notes do not carry the mode or Grow quarters do not show key projects and High-intensity work; then the text is not executed and the run says nothing about the hypothesis.
metadata.notes: Seed of a new family requested by the strategy session after the score-gap analysis; it is also the stall response for the cloud run's first block (leader posterior mean 61.34 -> 60.21 over three decisions). metadata.name: bold-1026-211845
metadata.hypothesis: Premise: fixed engine, judged stories. The small model misplays the champion's quarter-end judgement in repeatable ways, so take that judgement away: every quarter-end follows one stateless recipe that cannot pause growth for long, and all judgement goes into story choices, which move the statistics far more (lessons G5: v1 gained +44 Skill, +20 Network, +18 Output from stories against about +0, +4, +2 from Energy). Evidence from the champion's six digests. (1) Its risk state only ratchets up: the player never stepped down. scre-00003 took Lay low and reduce risk in 11 of 16 quarters, 10 in a row, including quarters that followed three calm HR remarks in a row, and refused new commitments in stories. At L3 its Skill and Network sat at their stall values (about 41 and 21) while Output, the only input still below its best, crept up about one point a quarter; it spent 18 months at L3 and finished at L4. ladd-00003 closed with 7 Lay-low quarters in a row and also finished at L4. The two L5 finishers took 6 and 2. (2) It reads 'weakest' as the smallest number. Before the first review ladd-00001 put two Energy points and the main action into Network while Network sat at its entry-level stall and Output was short; it was never promoted and was dismissed at month 24. (3) Its story rule pushes toward formal reports and escalations that cost the inputs a review reads: an anonymous HR report on a colleague and an open escalation over another team each cost two Network (ladd-00001, scre-00004), a formal written submission and a full incident response each cost Output, and ladd-00001 ended with Network at 0. Matteo's promotion study agrees: reviews are applied at the start of the review month, before its events and quarter-end, and at review time 11 of 15 unpromoted Haiku careers had dropped below their best on Network, Output or Skill, mostly through stories in the months just before the review. (4) The only careers past L5 (4 of 400 energy bots, Q 67-76) used a fixed quarter recipe with Apply for a key project every quarter and a Health point every quarter, and were promoted at each of their first three reviews. The recipe keeps G1 (Defuse after any risk wording, all career), G2 (a Health point most quarters, two when Health is low), G3 (Report results after a weak review, no Lay low), G4 (Output-first top-up) and G5 (honest ownership screens every story). What changes: risk is answered quarter by quarter, Lay low happens only at low Health or in the single quarter after strong risk wording, and the main action otherwise returns to Apply for a key project, the only published main action that raises Output, Skill and Network together. Why it should beat the champion: removing ratcheted Lay-low stretches keeps Output rising at L3 and L4, so completed careers reach L5 more often and earlier, lifting the level and wealth dimensions (46 and 34 for the champion, the two largest gaps). The story screens cut the pre-review losses of Network and Output that block first promotions, and promotion by the second review decides completion (12/14 completed when the first promotion came at the first review, 7/11 at the second, 0/13 later).
metadata.change: Replace the champion's single reactive Skill and its ratcheting Clear/Raised/Escalating state with three short Skills: a stateless quarter-end recipe (Health point, Defuse after any risk wording since the previous quarter-end, Output top-up, main action Apply for a key project unless Health is low, a weak review calls for Report results, or strong risk wording calls for one quarter of Lay low) and a story screen (honest ownership, then the Network cost of going against colleagues, then the Output cost of setting your own work aside, then Health and money).
metadata.predicted_behaviour: Notes at quarter-ends cite only feedback since the previous quarter-end and carry no Clear/Raised/Escalating label; about half of them say 'review next'. Main action: Apply for a key project in at least half of all quarters, Report results to your manager in the quarters after a C or D, Lay low and reduce risk in under a third of the champion's count and never for several quarters in a row while HR remarks are calm. Energy: Defuse legacy risk in every quarter whose preceding months carried risk wording, Health recovery in most quarters, Prepare report materials with the rest; no Skill learning or High-intensity work. Story notes name the Network or Output cost an option carries. Outcomes on race Haiku: completion at least the champion's (13 of 17), first promotion by the second review in most games, more than half of completed games at L5 or higher, completed level dimension above 46 and wealth above 34, risk control near the champion's 69.
metadata.refutation: Refuted if, with the same actor and environment, completion falls below the champion's, if trust-crisis exits or blow-ups per game rise (risk control of completed games clearly below 69), or if completed games do not end with higher level and wealth dimensions than 46 and 34. Manipulation check: if notes show a risk state kept across calm quarters, Lay low at comfortable Health after calm remarks, Skill learning or High-intensity work, or Apply for a key project in fewer than half of the quarters, the text was not followed and the result says nothing about the premise.
metadata.notes: fast race bold designer; premise: fixed engine, judged stories. A stateless quarter-end recipe modelled on the only careers that passed L5 (key project every quarter, Health point, Defuse on any risk wording), and all judgement moved into a short story screen. Brief premise 4 (separate quarter-end and story Skills), with guardrails G1-G5 kept. 632 words by wc -w including front matter (champion 393).

metadata.name: l1-review-clock-v1
metadata.idea_origin: Leah's local scripted sweep (1,562 games, lab/panel) and the race's score gap (lab/panel/README.md)
metadata.hypothesis: The race survives but does not grow: completed games average 13.8/30 on level and 6.9/20 on wealth, and over half of all eliminations are the capability dismissal after weak reviews. Leah's scripted sweep found that the best quarterly plan was a preventive Health reserve, then Prepare report materials, with Apply for a key project as the default main action, and that High-intensity work was the worst Energy choice. A manual that plans every quarter around the published review and promotion cadence, grows Skill, Network and Output together (the published promotion factors), keeps a Health reserve before it is needed and reads the HR remark as a risk gauge should promote earlier and more often than the reactive F3 leader, while surviving as often.
metadata.change: New single Skill, review-clock, about 390 words. Four rules: a preventive Health reserve in every Energy phase; the HR remark and warnings as a risk gauge driving Defuse legacy risk and Lay low; a window plan with Apply for a key project as the default main action, a catch-up action for whichever of Skill, Network or Output trails, Prepare report materials for spare Energy and no High-intensity work; story events judged on honest, scoped delivery versus hiding, blaming or overcommitting.
metadata.predicted_behaviour: Health stays in the upper part of its range in most quarters; Energy goes to Health recovery first and Prepare report materials second; High-intensity work never appears; Apply for a key project is the main action in most quarters; Defuse legacy risk follows a worried HR remark within the next Energy phase. Promotions arrive at the first or second window more often than in F3 runs, and the level dimension of completed games is higher than F3's.
metadata.refutation: Refuted if, with the same Haiku actor, the mean quantitative_score is below f3-feedback-reactive-v1's or the completion rate drops (growth bought with survival). Refuted on mechanism if the level dimension of completed games is not higher than F3's. The text is not being executed if High-intensity work appears, if notes stop naming the reserve, risk tone and window plan, or if Health is often in the lower part of its range at quarter end.
